$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=4{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)={x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t),\end{aligned}\,x(0)=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 5\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the initial value problem above. By applying the Laplace transform $L$ to both sides of each equation in our system, we get a system with variables ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$ In terms of the parameter $s,$ the solution of the new system is

${X}_{1}(s)=$ {{field-1}},
$\,{X}_{2}(s)=$ {{field-2}}.
worked_solution:
First, we find the Laplace transforms of both sides of each equation in our system:

$$
{\begin{aligned}L{{x}_{1}^{′}(t)}=L{4{x}_{1}(t)} \\ L{{x}_{2}^{′}(t)}=L{{x}_{1}(t)+3{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}\,\,
$$

Using the derivative property of the Laplace transform, we obtain the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}sL{{x}_{1}(t)}-{x}_{1}(0)=4L{{x}_{1}(t)} \\ sL{{x}_{2}(t)}-{x}_{2}(0)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}+3L{{x}_{2}(t)}\end{aligned}
$$

which can be simplified to:

$$
{\begin{aligned}s{X}_{1}(s)+2=4{X}_{1}(s) \\ s{X}_{2}(s)-5={X}_{1}(s)+3{X}_{2}(s)\end{aligned}
$$

where ${X}_{1}(s)=L{{x}_{1}(t)}$ and ${X}_{2}(s)=L{{x}_{2}(t)}.$

Now, solving the first equation for ${X}_{1}(s),$ we get

$$
s{X}_{1}(s)+2=4{X}_{1}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{1}(s)=-\frac{2}{s-4}.
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for ${X}_{2}(s)$ gives

$$
s{X}_{2}(s)-5=(-\frac{2}{s-4})+3{X}_{2}(s)\,⟹\,{X}_{2}(s)=\frac{5s-22}{(s-3)(s-4)}.
$$
